lots.guide_summary: Nothing same-item or close survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 close asking. The only external evidence is retail asking at GemSelect for larger (11 to 25ct) ammolites at about US$10 to US$22 per carat, which scaled to 6ct is about US$60 to US$130 (A$90 to A$200 at an approximate 1.52) ASKING, not sold. Gowans has sold no loose ammolite in the past year; generic single cabochons there make $10 to $27 hammer (category guide only, dropped as entries).
lots.working: No SOLD same-item or close evidence, so keep_max = 0 and flip_max = 0. For context only: Gowans single cabochons $10 to $27 hammer; retail asking scaled to 6ct A$90 to A$200. A realistic secondary-market value for a mid-grade 6ct ammolite is probably $40 to $100, but that is not supported by verified sales.
lots.confidence_reason: No sold or unsold comparables for ammolite; only retail asking for larger stones. No weight label, certificate or treatment information visible; 6ct and 'rare' are Gowans' words.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo, top view only. Pear cabochon with brown matrix and the crackled 'dragon skin' pattern typical of ammolite. Play of colour is patchy: bright green flashes upper left and lower right, red and orange patches centre, yellow flecks; large areas are dull brown with no colour. The edge shows brown shell/matrix with no visible glassy cap or layer line, so it looks like a solid or backed piece rather than a quartz-capped triplet, but the side and back are not shown so a doublet (backed) cannot be ruled out. Some fibres/dust on the surface. No weight or label visible on the jar.
lots.condition: Appears intact, no chips seen on the visible girdle; natural crackle lines across the face (normal for ammolite, but they are also where stability problems start). Colour grade looks mid to lower (mostly two colours with dead areas).
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you confirm the weight is 6ct and whether there is any certificate? Is it a solid ammolite or a doublet/triplet (please check the back and side for a black backing or clear quartz cap)?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all three researcher SOLD entries as comparables: 'BAG OF GREEN CABOCHON GEMSTONES' $24, 'TURQUOISE CABOCHON' $27 and 'MOONSTONE CABOCHON' $10 at Gowans. The figures are real (Gowans API, cabochon search, listed 2025-11-17/24) but they are different gems, so they cannot set a value or a bid for ammolite; mentioned in guide_summary as local context only. My own Gowans searches (ammolite, ammonite, rare gems, ct gemstone) found only fossils and silver-mounted ammonite pendants ($14 to $150), none a loose ammolite gem. WebSearch was not available (session search budget used up), so no auction results for ammolite were found; a follow-up search could add some.
lots.score_reason: Real but common gem; mid-grade colour; likely worth $40 to $100 retail-resale, and Gowans buyers pay little for loose cabochons.

lots.confidence_reason: Marks read for three pieces (lion passant salt spoon, two STERLING teaspoons) and the mustard spoon identified as plate, but weight unknown and only one photo-matched SOLD comparable (others matched on title).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2 (enlarged): salt spoon has a lion passant, a date letter (looks like I) and a worn maker/duty mark, so English sterling, probably Georgian or early Victorian. The mustard spoon's 'hallmarks' are a crowned shield with 'EP', '15', a cross-like mark and a gothic monogram, which are electroplate pseudo-hallmarks, not sterling. Photo 3: one teaspoon stamped STERLING with a small prefix, the other STERLING with a maple-leaf/lion style mark (likely Canadian). Photo 4: souvenir figural spoon marked WN with a small pseudo mark; silver content uncertain. Salt and mustard spoon bowls gilt (wear to gilding).
lots.condition: General wear, light tarnish and scratches; gilt bowls worn; no damage seen. Small, light pieces, probably 40 to 70g of sterling in total.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the total weight, and the weight of the hallmarked/STERLING pieces only? Is the souvenir spoon marked with any silver standard?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's aggregate entries '$80 to $100 hammer for small sterling groups' and '$5 to $35 for souvenir spoon bags' because they are ranges built from several lots, not single entries; replaced them with single verified lots (id 427323 $100 and id 372236 $20). All other researcher figures checked out in the Gowans API (prices, bids and listing dates match). Researcher's claim that the mustard spoon is hallmarked sterling is wrong: its marks are electroplate pseudo-hallmarks.
lots.score_reason: Three small sterling spoons, one plated, one souvenir; likely worth $30 to $80 at Gowans.

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD hammer at Gowans (no unsold, no asking). Close pairs of sterling spoons $210 (100g) to $360 (160.9g cased); category guides $40 to $490 cluster at about $2 per gram hammer. Value of lot 248 hangs on its weight: at $2/g a 100g pair is about $200 hammer, a 140g pair about $280. AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: keep_max: lowest surviving close SOLD pair = $210 (id 419289, 100g) / 1.198 = $175.29, rounded down to $175. This assumes lot 248 weighs at least about 100g; if Gowans says lighter, cap at about $1.75/g hammer. flip_max: likely resale = $210 x 1.198 = $251.58 all-in; less 13% selling fees = $218.87, less $12 outbound postage = $206.87; / 2.396 = $86.34, rounded down to $85. No silver melt figure (goldprice.org returned 403).
lots.confidence_reason: Hallmarks unread in the photos (Dublin and sterling rest on Gowans' title), weight unknown, and the close comparables are different patterns; supporting SOLD pages were opened.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: both spoons double-struck Kings/Queens pattern with shell and anthemion terminals and shell heel at the back of the bowl; a small tower crest engraved on each front terminal. Photo 2 (enlarged): a row of four marks plus a separate maker mark on each stem, too worn and small to read, consistent in layout with Dublin (crowned harp, Hibernia, date letter, maker) but not confirmed. Bowls look like dessert or table size against the tag.
lots.condition: Tarnish and staining/spotting inside both bowls, bowl wear and scratches; patterns crisp, no visible bends or splits. Worth a polish.
lots.question_for_gowans: What is the total weight of the pair, and can you confirm the hallmarks (Dublin, date letter, maker)? Are they table or dessert size?
lots.dropped_entries: No researcher figure was wrong on price or date (all match the Gowans API). Reclassified id 398105 ($60, 48.9g) from close to category guide because its photo shows a pair of Kings pattern sauce ladles, not spoons. Researcher's other category entries (Sargisons pair $110, teaspoon pair $40, 3 London spoons $230, 2 spoons 28.4g $100) are valid but small or makers' pieces, so I kept two representative ones and left the rest out as not adding anything. Added id 368691 ($360 cased 160.9g serving pair) and id 419435 ($490 for 6 dessert spoons 238.5g), both opened in the API. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget used), so no external Kings pattern or Dublin results.
lots.score_reason: A decent antique pair of patterned sterling spoons, likely $150 to $300 at Gowans depending on weight.
